summary: In this excerpt from Book 2, the narrator is recruited by Checker to provide backup for Arthur Tresting, who has gone alone to confront Dawna Polk in the Los Angeles desert after her tracker reactivated in a suspicious setup. Checker explains Tresting left hours earlier against his advice, refusing to involve others out of a sense of nobility. The narrator agrees to help immediately, reflecting on feeling isolated and expendable, and ends by promising to hurry to the location.
one_line: Checker recruits the narrator to back up Arthur Tresting, who is heading alone into a likely trap to find Dawna Polk in Los Angeles.
key_facts: Checker asks the narrator for backup for Arthur, saying Arthur 'needs backup' and would not like Checker asking.
Polk's tracker came back on, with the signal located in Los Angeles.
The narrator suspects Polk's tracker was found by her captors, making the reappearance a possible setup.
Tresting has decided to go in tonight despite expecting that the people behind Polk are waiting for him.
Checker says satellite imagery only shows some buildings in the middle of the desert.
Checker texts the narrator the location and tracker frequency details.
Tresting left a few hours before the call, and Checker says he tried to stop him.
Tresting refused to call in help, with Checker describing him as having an 'idiotic nobility complex' about not involving anyone else.
The narrator believes Tresting had another reason for not calling him, which makes the narrator eager to save him again.
Checker asks whether it is true what Dawna Polk can do, and the narrator replies, 'Yeah. I'm pretty sure it is.'
The narrator reflects that no one would miss him if he made a suicide run and he would disappear into the Los Angeles underground.
The narrator says 'I'm on my way' and Checker thanks him, saying he owes him big.
